q: What currency is used in Bihać, Bosnia?
a: Bihać and the whole of Bosnia and Herzegovina use the convertible mark, abbreviated KM (currency code BAM). One mark has 100 fening. Coins range from 5 fening to 5 KM and notes from 10 to 200 KM. Receipts and price lists show KM, while banks and exchange-rate boards use BAM.

q: How much is 1 euro in Bosnian marks?
a: The convertible mark is pegged to the euro at a fixed rate of 1 euro = 1.95583 KM. In practice people often reckon 1 euro is roughly 2 KM, or that 1 KM is just over 50 euro cents. Exchange offices and banks offer a slightly less favourable buying rate than the official one.

q: Does the Bosnian mark exchange rate against the euro change?
a: No, the rate has been fixed since the euro was introduced and stands at 1.95583 KM to 1 euro. So there is no need to watch the exchange rate before your trip. Differences only arise from the commission and rates applied by individual exchange offices, banks and shops that accept euros. Thanks to the fixed rate, you can easily convert prices in marks to euros by dividing by two.

q: Can I pay in euros in Bihać?
a: Many places in Bihać accept euros, especially accommodation, larger restaurants and petrol stations, but it is not guaranteed. When you pay in euros, you usually get your change in marks at a rounded rate of about 2 KM. For coffee, bakeries, the market and parking it is better to have marks.

q: What exchange rate do shops in Bosnia use when you pay in euros?
a: Shops and restaurants that accept euros usually count 1 euro as 2 KM or slightly less and give change in marks. For you this is normally a little worse than the official rate of 1.95583. For larger amounts it is worth paying by card or withdrawing marks from a cash machine.

q: Can I pay for accommodation in Bihać in euros?
a: Accommodation prices on apartmanibihac.com are given in euros, from €25 to €100 per night for the whole property, depending on the property and the season. You pay in cash on arrival, with no compulsory deposit. Whether you pay in euros or marks is confirmed by the owner in the reply to your enquiry.

q: Are cards accepted in Bihać?
a: Yes, Visa and Mastercard are accepted in most supermarkets, petrol stations, hotels and larger restaurants in Bihać. Smaller cafés, bakeries, the market and some private landlords prefer cash. So always carry some marks as well as your card. At the market and with small traders, cash is still the safest way to pay.

q: Can I use American Express in Bosnia?
a: American Express is accepted much less often in Bosnia and Herzegovina than Visa and Mastercard. In smaller places such as Bihać, expect many businesses not to take it. Bring a Visa or Mastercard and some cash. Before you travel, check with your bank whether it charges a fee for card payments outside the EU.

q: Are there cash machines in Bihać?
a: Yes, there are plenty of cash machines in Bihać, especially in the town centre, at banks and shopping centres. In smaller villages along the Una, such as Grmuša or Lohovo, there are hardly any, so withdraw money in town. Cash machines dispense convertible marks. Plan your withdrawals before heading out on a river trip or rafting.

q: Do cash machines in Bosnia charge fees for foreign cards?
a: Many cash machines in Bosnia charge a fee for withdrawals with a foreign card, and your own bank may charge one too. The amount depends on the bank and is usually shown on screen before you confirm. If the machine asks whether you want conversion into your home currency, decline and choose to be paid in marks.

q: Should I pay in euros or marks when my card is charged in Bosnia?
a: Choose marks when a card terminal or cash machine offers to charge you in euros instead of marks. Dynamic currency conversion (DCC) at the point of sale usually has a worse rate than the one your bank applies. Paying in the local currency is normally cheaper. The same rule applies to card payments in shops and to cash withdrawals.

q: Where can I exchange money in Bihać?
a: You can exchange money at banks and licensed exchange offices in the centre of Bihać, and some post offices also exchange currency. Because of the fixed peg, the euro rate is stable and there is little difference between exchange offices. Do not change money with strangers on the street. Bring your ID card or passport, as the bank may ask for it.

q: Should I buy Bosnian marks before I travel?
a: Generally not, as your bank at home may offer a worse rate for marks than you would get in Bosnia. The simplest option is to bring euros and exchange them in Bihać or withdraw marks from a cash machine. Since the rate is fixed, there is no point waiting for a better moment.

q: Can I change Bosnian marks back into euros at the end of my holiday?
a: Yes, you can change leftover marks back into euros at banks and exchange offices in Bosnia. Outside Bosnia and Herzegovina marks are hard to exchange, so do it before you leave the country. It is best to spend your cash towards the end of your stay and pay the rest by card.

q: How much does a coffee cost in Bihać?
a: A coffee in a café in Bihać usually costs roughly 2 to 3.5 KM, or about €1 to €1.80. Prices depend on the location, so they are a little higher in the centre and by the river. That is noticeably cheaper than in Croatia or Western Europe.

q: How much does a meal at a restaurant in Bihać cost?
a: A main course at an ordinary restaurant in Bihać usually costs roughly 12 to 25 KM, or about €6 to €13. Fish from the Una, a mixed grill for several people or dishes at upmarket restaurants can be more expensive. Portions are usually large, so one dish is often enough for a meal.

q: How much do ćevapi cost in Bihać?
a: A portion of ćevapi in Bihać usually costs roughly 6 to 12 KM, depending on the size and the place. They come with somun flatbread and onions, while kajmak is often charged separately. Exact prices are always on the menu, so check before you order.

q: How much is petrol in Bosnia and Herzegovina?
a: Fuel prices in Bosnia change almost every week and vary between petrol stations, so we do not quote them here as a fixed figure. You will see current prices at the stations and on local websites that track fuel prices. You can pay by card at petrol stations, and often in euros as well.

q: Is petrol cheaper in Bosnia than in Croatia?
a: Historically, fuel in Bosnia has often been somewhat cheaper than in Croatia, but the difference changes with the market and price regulations. Before you travel, compare current prices on websites that track fuel prices in both countries. At the Izačić crossing many drivers fill up on whichever side of the border is cheaper at the time.

q: Is Bosnia and Herzegovina cheap for tourists?
a: For most visitors from the EU, Bosnia and Herzegovina is noticeably cheaper than Croatia, Austria or Germany, especially for food, coffee and accommodation. Imported goods in shops and fuel are not much cheaper. On apartmanibihac.com a whole apartment costs from €25 (50 KM) per night, roughly what a single room for one person costs in Bihać.

q: How much money do I need for a weekend in Bihać?
a: For two people, budget roughly €50 to €100 a day for food, coffee and smaller trips, excluding accommodation. Add rafting, Una National Park tickets and fuel separately, depending on your plans. For accommodation, a whole apartment on apartmanibihac.com costs from €25 (50 KM) per night.

q: How much should I tip in restaurants in Bosnia?
a: Tipping in restaurants in Bosnia and Herzegovina is not compulsory, but it is customary if you are happy with the service. Most people round up the bill or leave about 10 %. In cafés people usually leave small change or round up to the nearest round figure. You can tip in cash, in either marks or euros.

q: Do you tip taxi drivers in Bihać?
a: A tip is not expected, but people often round up to the nearest round figure. Agree the fare before the journey or check that the meter is running. Short trips within Bihać are usually cheap. For longer journeys, for example to Grmuša or the border, always agree the price in advance, as the meter is not always used then.

q: How much is the entrance fee for Una National Park?
a: Ticket prices for Una National Park vary by location (Štrbački buk, Martin Brod) and visitor category, and change from season to season. Check current prices on the park's official website, npuna.com. According to the park's price list, you pay in cash or by bank transfer, so it is a good idea to have marks in cash at the entrance.

q: How much does rafting on the Una river cost?
a: The price of rafting depends on the section, the duration and what is included, such as lunch or transport. We organise rafting with Una Olympic Rafting from Grmuša, so we can send you an exact offer for your date on request. Message us on WhatsApp or Viber at +387 61 591 320.

q: Can I pay for rafting on the Una in euros?
a: Rafting operators on the Una usually accept both euros and marks, and some take cards too. For rafting with Una Olympic Rafting, which we arrange alongside our accommodation, we confirm the payment method with the offer. Contact us on +387 61 591 320 or send an enquiry on apartmanibihac.com.

q: Is Bosnia part of EU roaming?
a: No, Bosnia and Herzegovina is not an EU member and is not in the roam-like-at-home zone. Calls and mobile data with an EU SIM card can be expensive, depending on your provider. In 2026 the EU started negotiations on including the Western Balkans in its roaming area, but this is not yet in force.

q: How much does it cost to use my EU phone in Bosnia?
a: It depends on your provider and tariff, as Bosnia is not in the EU roaming zone. Some European providers offer special bundles for Bosnia, so ask yours before you travel. Without a bundle, mobile data can quickly become expensive, so switch off data roaming until you have checked the prices.

q: How can I avoid a high phone bill in Bosnia?
a: Before you travel, check your provider's prices and any bundles for Bosnia, and switch off data roaming on your phone. Use the Wi-Fi at your accommodation, which is free at most properties. For a longer stay it is worth buying a local SIM card or a tourist eSIM.

q: Can I buy a local SIM card in Bihać?
a: Yes, you can buy a prepaid SIM card at operator shops, kiosks and some stores in Bihać. The main operators are BH Telecom, m:tel and HT Eronet, and all of them cover Bihać. Some offer tourist packages with plenty of mobile data for a few days.

q: How much is a tourist SIM card in Bosnia?
a: Tourist data packages from operators in Bosnia usually cost roughly 20 to 60 KM, depending on the amount of data and the validity. Offers change often, so check them on the operators' websites or in store. For a short stay, a tourist eSIM may also be cheaper.

q: Can I use an eSIM in Bosnia and Herzegovina?
a: Yes, eSIMs work in Bosnia, offered both by local operators and by international tourist eSIM providers. A tourist eSIM usually includes data only, without a local number. Check that your phone supports eSIM before buying. A local SIM card is usually better value if you also need calls, while an eSIM is more convenient because you can activate it before you arrive.

q: Is food in Bosnian supermarkets cheaper than in Croatia?
a: Local products such as bread, dairy, fruit and vegetables are generally somewhat cheaper than in Croatia. Imported branded goods often cost about the same or even more. Seasonal fruit and vegetables are usually cheapest at the market in Bihać. Large supermarket chains and the market are in Bihać itself, while the villages along the Una only have small shops.

q: Are there large supermarkets in Bihać?
a: Yes, there are large supermarkets and chain stores in Bihać where you can pay by card. They have a wide range of food, drinks and toiletries at prices typical for Bosnia. The villages along the Una only have small shops, so do your big shop in town.

q: How much is a beer in a bar in Bihać?
a: A local beer in a café or bar in Bihać usually costs roughly 3 to 5 KM, with imported beers a little more. Prices depend on the place and the size of the bottle or glass. Beer is much cheaper in shops than in bars. Local rakija is also popular in Bihać, and its price likewise depends on the place.

q: Is there a tourist tax in Bihać?
a: Yes, tourists in Bosnia generally pay a tourist tax, the amount of which is set by the canton and the town. With us it is usually charged together with the accommodation price, and the owner will tell you whether it is included. Ask about it in your enquiry on apartmanibihac.com to avoid surprises.

q: How much does accommodation in Bihać cost per night?
a: A single room for one person in Bihać usually costs about 50 KM per night. On apartmanibihac.com, for roughly the same amount, from €25 or 50 KM, you get a whole apartment, some of them up to 100 m². Prices range from €25 to €100 per night for the whole property, depending on the property and the season.

q: Is it worth renting a whole apartment instead of a room in Bihać?
a: Yes, because a whole apartment on apartmanibihac.com costs from €25 (50 KM) per night, which is what a single room for one person usually costs in Bihać. For that price you get a kitchen, your own bathroom and more space, and some apartments are up to 100 m². For a couple or a family the price per person is even lower.

q: Do I have to pay a deposit for accommodation in Bihać?
a: No, with us there is no compulsory deposit: you pay in cash on arrival. If you wish, you can pay in advance and receive a discount for doing so; the discount and payment method are agreed when your enquiry is confirmed. There is no booking fee, and confirmation arrives by e-mail.

q: Is Bihać more expensive in summer than in winter?
a: Accommodation is usually more expensive in summer, as that is the main season for rafting, swimming in the Una and trips to Plitvice. Food and coffee in town generally cost the same all year round. On apartmanibihac.com the nightly price depends on the property and the season, from €25 to €100 for the whole property.
